lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The triage-backlog result is repeated in two entries with different reductions.
items.because: The Mobility Systems bullet says 68%, while the framework bullet says two-thirds, leaving the figure and project attribution unclear.

items.says: The 35% accuracy change lacks a baseline and accuracy measure.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the change represents or compare it.

items.says: The tool-call and latency results appear after the training method.
items.because: Readers reach the method before the impact, making the outcomes harder to scan.

items.says: Two Mobility Systems bullets appear to claim the same adapter fine-tuning as separate achievements.
items.because: Both mention assistant-only loss masking, and this bullet adds no distinct result beyond the accuracy improvement.

items.says: Switching from FP32 to BF16 does not by itself explain a 4x reduction in total GPU memory.
items.because: BF16 halves storage for values stored in it, while gradients and optimizer state may still use FP32.

items.says: “For fine-tuning the perception models” is wordier than needed.
items.because: A shorter phrase would leave more room for the result.

items.says: The 200 ms build gate does not establish the stated 420 ms-to-180 ms p95 change.
items.because: It shows only that a tested run stayed under 200 ms, not the exact result, comparable baseline, or effects of caching and batching.

items.says: The trailing load-test clause is longer than needed to state the build gate.
items.because: A shorter description would preserve the check and make the bullet quicker to scan.

items.says: The bullet switches from past-tense “Maintained” to present-tense “adds.”
items.because: The role ended in July 2024, so the tense shift can make the work sound ongoing.

items.says: The three-day release cycle lacks the previous duration.
items.because: Readers cannot judge how much shorter the cycle became.

items.says: The release-cycle result comes after the methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the outcome behind the pipeline and regression-check details.

items.says: “Maintained the CI pipeline” describes a responsibility rather than a specific action.
items.because: It does not show what was done to the pipeline.

items.says: The backlog result gives no measure of backlog volume or dispatch delay.
items.because: Readers can see that dispatch improved but not the scale of the problem addressed.

items.says: The clause about delayed morning dispatch adds length after the outcome is clear.
items.because: “Removing the nightly backlogs” already states the result, and the clause does not measure the impact.

items.says: The bullet does not show how removal of failures was verified under 50-way fan-out.
items.because: The load condition does not show whether the fix was tested or how reliably it prevented failures.

items.says: The result follows both implementation details.
items.because: Readers encounter the changes before learning that they removed deadlocks and lost tool results.

items.says: The AI-practices impact is generic and shows no specific contribution.
items.because: The bullet says neither what changed nor what was done to drive adoption.

items.says: The metrics integration gives no resulting change or evidence of use.
items.because: The count shows the contribution’s scope but not its value.

items.says: The Kendall correlation does not identify the two quantities being correlated.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the correlation demonstrates.

items.says: The correlation result comes after the trial details.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the trial conditions before the key outcome.

items.says: The backlog result is attributed to the evaluation-framework project despite being attributed elsewhere to the internship.
items.because: The résumé does not establish that the industrial sensor-triage work belonged to the framework.
